html:
Jonas Savimbi was the founder and leader of UNITA, the rebel movement that fought Portuguese rule and then the MPLA government of Angola, from 1966 until he was killed in 2002.

An Ovimbundu from the central highlands, he studied in Portugal and Switzerland. He changed his ideas to suit his allies, moving from Maoism to anti-communism, and won backing from South Africa and the United States, where President Reagan received him.

He refused to accept his defeat in the 1992 election, and his return to war was among the deadliest phases of the civil war, paid for by highland diamonds sold in breach of sanctions. He was killed by government troops in Moxico in February 2002, and peace came weeks later in Angola.
